newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Air sees creditors liking plan.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Air sees creditors liking plan.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp chief executive Kevin Benson said on Friday that developments in the company's survival strategy over the past eight hours, including the winning over of a major union, would help it gain the confidence of creditors.

Benson, set to start a series of meetings with creditors around the world on Saturday to appeal for time to make payment obligations, was buoyed by news of the Canadian Union of Public Employees' agreement to support the package.
"I think they will be delighted to hear this morning's news. I think we're in good standing," he told a news conference.

CUPE, which represents 2,700 flight attendants at Canadian, agreed earlier today to support a restructuring plan after British Columbia Premier Glen Clark offered to add C$3.1 million to its C$8 million annual concession contribution.
Canadian, however, still required the support of the Canadian Auto Workers, which remained opposed to wage cuts for employees.

Benson stressed that the deal, which now includes employee wage concessions totaling C$31.9 million and government tax breaks and other savings totaling C$38.1 million, still required approval from all six unions for all the pieces to fall into place.

"We do need the CAW on board and I ask and entreat them again to come on board," he said, adding that in the past week, Canadian had garnered new support from CUPE and the International Association of Machinists and won concessions from the governments of Canada, Alberta and B.C.
Benson said he would continue to negotiate with the CAW to attempt to win its support. "Give us a couple more days and let's see where we can go," he said.
He said a number of the company's creditors had already given it a moratorium on payments while it completed its life-support proposal.
With the obligations due on Saturday the carrier hopes to have deferred total C$18 million to C$20 million, Benson said.

At the news conference, which included union leaders, B.C.'s Clark stressed the impact that Canadian has on his provincial economy and strategic importance of Vancouver to Canadian and AMR Corp. unit American Airlines as a gateway hub to the rich Asian market. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
